title: Rendering pipeline and Core Animation
summary: Your app builds a tree of layers and sends it to a system render server, which draws it with the GPU. Stutters come either from slow work in your app (commit) or from expensive layer effects (render).
body: **In simple words:** Every `UIView` has a `CALayer` underneath. When something changes, your app (on the main thread) does layout, drawing and image decoding, then "commits" the layer tree. A separate process (the render server) turns that into pixels with the GPU.
**Steps per frame:** Event (touch) → Commit in your app (layout, display/`draw(_:)`, prepare such as image decoding, send) → Render server prepares and renders → Display.
**Commit hitch (your code is slow):** heavy layout, big Auto Layout changes, decoding large images on main, `draw(_:)` doing a lot.

**Render hitch (layers are expensive):** offscreen passes caused by shadows without `shadowPath`, `cornerRadius` + `masksToBounds` on complex content, group opacity, blurs. Fix with `shadowPath`, simpler masks, pre-rendered images.

**Image decoding:** `UIImage(named:)` and `UIImage(data:)` decode lazily, on first draw, on main. Decode/downsample in the background (`preparingForDisplay()`, `byPreparingThumbnail(ofSize:)`, ImageIO). A 4000×3000 photo uses ~48 MB when decoded, even if the file is 2 MB.
**Animations** run in the render server, so they stay smooth even if main is briefly busy.
keyPoints: UIView is backed by CALayer; the render server draws the committed layer tree on the GPU.
Commit hitches = app main-thread work; render hitches = expensive layer effects.
Avoid offscreen rendering: set `shadowPath`, avoid masks on complex content.
Decode and downsample images off main; decoded size = width × height × 4 bytes.
Measure with Instruments Animation Hitches and Organizer hitch metrics.

mistakes: Setting large images directly into small image views.
followups: **What is offscreen rendering?** The GPU must render into a separate buffer first (for masks, shadows) and then composite - extra passes per frame.
**UIView vs CALayer?** CALayer handles drawing and animation; UIView adds touch handling, layout and the responder chain.
